Title: Supplier payments taken through the Pay Supplier form are not allocated to GRN obligations, so the GRN pay screen keeps offering the full bill and the same money can be paid twice
Environment: Isolated copy of AMSV5-2_FIXED on SQLite (86 tables, 618 routes); Admin session; no production data touched.
Preconditions / test data: GRN-1: 1,000 kg 12mm + 500 kg 20mm, material obligation 160,000. GRN-2: 400 kg, 44,000.
Reproduction steps:
1) Pay 60,000 from the Pay Supplier form against supplier R2-SUP-01.
2) Read /api/supplier_balance/1 (100,000).
3) Read /accounts/api/supplier_open_obligations/1 and /accounts/api/pay_grn/1 (MATERIAL:1 still 160,000).
4) Pay MATERIAL:1 in full from the GRN pay screen.
Expected result: After step 1 the GRN pay screen offers only the 100,000 still owed; step 4 is refused or warns.
Actual result (evidence): Step 1: cash -60,000, supplier ledger 204,000 -> 144,000, but MATERIAL:1 still shows paid 0.00 / remaining 160,000 and the drop-down reads 'stock due 160,000.00'. Step 4 succeeded: cash -160,000 and the supplier balance fell from 100,000 to -60,000 (a credit the supplier never earned).
Impact: The shop can pay 60,000 twice for one delivery note. The supplier ledger and cash stay internally consistent (so nothing looks broken), the money is simply gone until the supplier refunds it.
Suspected cause: grn_costing.supplier_obligation_paid_minor() only sees payments attributed to a GRN (supplier_payment.source_type='GRN_PAYMENT'); /add_supplier_payment writes a voucher with source_type/source_id NULL, and the report layer (/accounts/purchase_payables) nets it while the GRN screens do not.

Title: Voiding a sale that already has a material return counts the returned goods twice: phantom stock and a client credit that is never reversed
Environment: Isolated copy of AMSV5-2_FIXED; Admin session.
Preconditions / test data: Credit sale SB-SL-1004: 200 kg 20mm at 160 = 32,000; 10,000 received; 20 kg returned (3,200).
Reproduction steps:
1) Void the credit sale after the return.
2) Read the 20mm stock, the stock entries and the client ledger.
Expected result: The 200 kg delivered comes back once: stock returns to the physical 500 kg, and the client is owed back only the 35,000 they actually paid (5,000 opening settled).
Actual result (evidence): Stock went 320 -> 520 kg: the voided OUT entry restores 200 while the return entry had already restored 20, so 520 instead of 500 kg. The return credit of 3,200 stayed on the client ledger: net -38,200 instead of -35,000. The P&L export then quotes earned revenue 35,800 while the net profit is computed from 39,000.
Impact: Stock is overstated and the shop owes the customer 3,200 it has already given back in goods. The error is invisible on screen because every total is internally consistent.
Suspected cause: The void path reverses the sale's stock entry and its receivable, but never looks for material_return rows pointing at the sale (material_return.source_sale_id), so their stock and credit entries survive.

Title: An expense recorded through the Accounts expense form cannot be voided or deleted: the request dies on a foreign-key constraint and the operator only sees a generic 'data error'
Environment: Isolated copy of AMSV5-2_FIXED; Admin session.
Preconditions / test data: 3,000 shop rent posted from /accounts/transactions/new (pay_target=personal_expense, category + payee).
Reproduction steps:
1) POST the void route for that voucher (with or without a reason).
2) Read the account transaction and the cash balance.
Expected result: The voucher is reversed (cash back to where it was) and kept as a void document, like every other module.
Actual result (evidence): HTTP 200 with the flash 'The operation could not be completed due to a data error. No changes were saved'. Server log: sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError FOREIGN KEY constraint failed on DELETE FROM account_transaction WHERE id = ?. Cash unchanged, voucher still live.
Impact: A wrong expense can only be corrected by editing the amount (which works), never removed; an expense posted to the wrong account or by the wrong user has no reversal path at all.
Suspected cause: cash_flow_svc.void_manual_cash_flow_entry() deletes the AccountTransaction (line 1367) before the CashFlowEntry that references it through cash_flow_entry.account_tx_id (line 1370).

Title: GET /logs dies with an AttributeError for an anonymous visitor instead of redirecting to the login page
Environment: Isolated copy of AMSV5-2_FIXED; no session.
Reproduction steps:
1) Request /logs without a cookie.
2) Compare with /settings or /system_report.
Expected result: 302 to /login?next=/logs like every other protected page.
Actual result (evidence): AttributeError: 'AnonymousUserMixin' object has no attribute 'role' — the request never reaches a redirect and the browser gets a 500 page.
Impact: Broken page for anyone hitting a stale bookmark or a shared link; the login redirect that should guide them never appears. No data is exposed.
Suspected cause: app/blueprints/system/logs.py::_guard() reads current_user.role before any authentication check, and the routes carry no @login_required.

Title: A newly created user with the default (all-zero) permissions is stuck in an infinite redirect loop
Preconditions / test data: Admin creates a second user (role=user) and ticks nothing — the form stores every can_* flag as 0.
Reproduction steps:
1) Log in as the new user.
2) Open / .
Expected result: A page that explains the account has no access yet, or a redirect to a page that does.
Actual result (evidence): 302 to / for ever (browser: ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS). Granting one permission (can_view_dashboard) makes / return 200, so the loop is the 'no permission' branch of the dashboard guard.
Impact: Every user must be created and then fixed in a second step; a half-configured account looks like a dead application to its owner.
Suspected cause: The dashboard guard redirects to index when the user lacks can_view_dashboard; index is the same page, so the guard re-fires with no terminal branch.

Title: An under-collected counter sale to a free-text walk-in name creates a receivable that belongs to no client, so no ledger can show it and Current Payables reports zero
Preconditions / test data: Counter sale to 'R2 Walk-in' (not in the client master), 7,500 bill, 5,000 collected.
Reproduction steps:
1) Save the sale (flash: 'Rs. 2,500.00 shown as unpaid instead of rejecting it — collect it from the client ledger').
2) Open /current_payables, the client list and the system report.
Expected result: The bill is either attached to a client record or the operator is told it cannot be chased.
Actual result (evidence): pending_bill SB-SL-1003 (3,000) exists with client_name 'R2 Walk-in' and no client row; /current_payables lists 0 clients and Rs. 0.00; the system report counts 3 unpaid bills. The flash sends the operator to a ledger that has no such client.
Impact: Money owed by a walk-in can never be chased from the UI; the receivable exists only as a row in a table nobody reads. Any walk-in short payment is silently lost.
Suspected cause: The direct-sale writer creates a pending_bill for the shortfall but only creates/links a client master row on some paths; every ledger and payables view then joins on client master and drops the bill.

Title: Cancelling a booking rewrites the booking total to zero and deletes its item lines, so the order content survives only in the ledger text
Preconditions / test data: Booking D: 100 kg 20mm at 150 = 15,000, paid in full in advance; bookings B and C undelivered.
Reproduction steps:
1) Cancel the client's remaining bookings.
2) Inspect booking D and its booking_item rows.
Expected result: The cancellation is recorded without destroying what was ordered (or the original rows are archived).
Actual result (evidence): booking.amount 15,000 -> 0.00, is_void stays 0, and the booking_item rows are gone (1 -> 0). The activity log keeps an 'Edited Booking ... (1 field: amount) Rs 0' entry and the client ledger keeps 'Booking Return/Cancel (R2 12mm Steel Bar)', so the material name survives but not the quantity or rate.
Impact: A disputed cancellation cannot be reconstructed from the document; the money is right.
Suspected cause: The cancel plan rewrites the booking to its undelivered remainder (0) and drops the item lines instead of flagging the booking cancelled.

Title: A non-numeric opening balance is accepted silently and stored as zero, with a success message
Reproduction steps:
1) Create a client with opening_balance='abc'.
2) Read the client row and the flash.
Expected result: Refused: an opening balance is money and cannot be skipped silently.
Actual result (evidence): Client created, opening_balance 0.0, flash 'Client Registered'. Nothing tells the operator the 5,000/10,000 they typed was dropped.
Impact: Opening balances are the only way to bring a running book into the system; a silently zeroed balance understates receivables from day one.
Suspected cause: The client form coerces with a numeric parse that falls back to 0 instead of raising.

Title: The P&L workbook quotes a revenue figure that its own net profit is not computed from once an orphan return exists
Environment: Isolated copy of AMSV5-2_FIXED; after the return-against-voided-sale scenario.
Reproduction steps:
1) Download the P&L workbook.
2) Compare 'Earned Material Revenue (net of returns)' with 'Net Profit / Loss' minus the COGS and expense lines.
Expected result: The Summary sheet adds up: revenue - COGS - operating expenses = net profit.
Actual result (evidence): Earned Material Revenue 35,800, COGS 25,468.75, Operating Expenses 3,500, reported net 10,031.25 — the sheet's own revenue line would give 6,831.25. The net is computed from 39,000; the 3,200 return is subtracted twice (once from revenue, once excluded as 'Unresolved Revenue Excluded From Net').
Impact: Two revenue figures in one workbook; a reader who starts from the revenue line cannot reproduce the profit.
Suspected cause: The orphan return (F-R2-02) has no sale to reverse, so the export classifies it as unresolved revenue but the net-profit engine still uses the gross base.

Title: No screen in the application reports the value of stock on hand
Preconditions / test data: 1,400 kg of 12mm bought in two batches (101.875 and 120.00 per kg landed).
Reproduction steps: 1) Look for a closing-stock or inventory-value figure on every inventory and report screen.
Expected result: A trading shop can read what its stock is worth at cost.
Actual result (evidence): Stock Summary shows quantities only; the material ledger shows movements; the P&L is COGS-only. The 149,875 of landed inventory is nowhere on any screen (material.unit_price is a sale price and stays 0).
Impact: Buying and pricing decisions run blind on inventory value; no balance-sheet-style check of stock against cash is possible.
Suspected cause: Only quantities are projected; the landed cost per grn_item is used for COGS at delivery time and is never aggregated into a stock valuation.

Title: The dashboard's 'Total Outstanding — real dues across open bills' reads zero while three bills worth 17,500 are open
Preconditions / test data: AC01 has two open booking bills (11,500 + 3,000) and a 15,000 unallocated advance; a walk-in bill of 3,000 has no client.
Reproduction steps:
1) Read the Total Outstanding tile.
2) Read /current_payables and the pending-bill table.
Expected result: The tile either shows the collectable amount or says plainly that it is a net ledger balance.
Actual result (evidence): Tile 0.00; /current_payables 0.00 / 0 clients; pending_bill holds 17,500 across 3 unpaid bills and the system report counts them ('3 Unpaid Bills').
Impact: The owner sees 'nothing to collect' while 17,500 is open. Unallocated advances hide real bills and the ownerless walk-in bill is invisible everywhere.
Suspected cause: The tile is the sum of client ledger net balances (debit side only); advances are not applied to bills and bills without a client master are not in any ledger.

Title: Booking-delivery cost of goods is labelled 'Estimated Material Cost' even though the delivery line carries the frozen landed cost
Preconditions / test data: 100 kg of 12mm delivered against a booking, cost_rate_at_sale = 101.875 on the delivery line.
Reproduction steps: 1) Read the P&L export lines 'Actual Recorded Material Cost' and 'Estimated Material Cost'.
Expected result: Cost taken from a frozen cost_rate_at_sale counts as recorded, not estimated.
Actual result (evidence): 15,281.25 recorded / 10,187.50 estimated: the 10,187.50 is exactly 100 x 101.875, i.e. the frozen cost. The page also says '2 estimated-cost rows'.
Impact: Cosmetic but it undermines trust in the profit figure: a reader is warned that half the cost of goods is a guess when it is not.
Suspected cause: The estimator flag is set for lines whose source document is a booking delivery instead of being driven by the presence of cost_rate_at_sale.

Title: PDF exports need the optional requirements-pdf.txt; the shipped environment lacks it and the screen degrades with a clear message
Reproduction steps:
1) Download the P&L PDF.
2) Install requirements-pdf.txt and repeat.
Expected result: Either the exports work out of the box or the deployment notes say they need the extra file.
Actual result (evidence): Before: 302 + 'PDF export is unavailable. Install requirements-pdf.txt and restart the app.' After installing: 200, application/pdf, 61,308 bytes starting %PDF. Excel and the ledger CSVs work either way.
Impact: Deployment gap only; the app never pretends the file was produced.
Suspected cause: Optional dependency, correctly detected at runtime.

Title: Cancelling a booking is client-wide (LIFO), not per booking
Preconditions / test data: Client AC01 with three undelivered bookings (B, C, D).
Reproduction steps:
1) Post the cancel for client AC01.
2) Count the cancelled bookings.
Expected result: Either one booking or all of them — as long as the screen says which.
Actual result (evidence): All three went at once: flash 'Total cancelled: 200.00 items, value 30000.00'.
Impact: The page already previews 'Cancel Remaining Booking (LIFO)', so this is documented behaviour; it is recorded because a per-booking cancel does not exist.
Suspected cause: The route is client-scoped by design.
